Student-led protests over education

in several European countries this weekend.
In France, where protests have been taking place for weeks,
police used water cannons and tear gas Saturday
to disperse some more violent demonstrators.
But NPR's Eleanor Beardsley says
many of those protesting were not attacking police officers.
I would say France was like a split screen,

Lots of students, remember it began with their demand

But it's now been joined by a lot of public sector workers,
firefighters, hospital workers, unions,
angry over high prices, low wages,
and what they call general inequality.
And there were horrible scenes of chaos and violence today.
That's NPR's Eleanor Beardsley with our story.
President Trump was in Northern Kentucky today
as part of an effort to rally Republican voters.
His visit comes as opponents have their own
get out to vote activities.
Member Station WVXU's Bill Reinhardt has more.
Members of the No Kings movement
are trying to keep their message nonpartisan.
Local Democratic activist Crimson McDonald
brought coffee and cookies to people
demonstrating outside the Trump rally.
She says partisanship is dead.
People are gonna turn out this election,
and it's not gonna be for the Democrats.
It's not gonna be for the Republicans.
It's gonna be for common sense policy,
and it's gonna be for politicians
that are ready to fight for us
to make our life and our quality of life better.
McDonald says she expects high voter turnout next month
because of high prices.
She says Americans will realize
the only power they have is at the ballot box.
For NPR News, I'm Bill Reinhardt in Cincinnati.
Fire crews appear to be making some progress today
as they try to contain a wildfire south of Los Angeles.
The Norte fire has burned at least 570 acres.
And so far, officials say it's now 25% contained.
Steve Futterman has our reports.
Overnight, fire crews here made progress.
The Santa Ana winds have not gone away,
but they are not nearly as strong as Friday.
That's good news for firefighters.
Steve Concialdi is a captain
with the Orange County Fire Authority.
He says drones are helping to pinpoint dangerous areas.
They can pinpoint where the hot spots are,
and they'll tell all our firefighters where to go there,
and we put water on it.
Officials say when the weather forecast earlier this week
predicted strong winds,
they prepositioned fire crews and equipment.
It paid off.
As soon as the Norte fire broke out,
they were able to quickly respond.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman
in San Juan Capistrano, California.
The Henderson fire, meanwhile,
is continuing to burn near Camp Pendleton,
which is located in northern San Diego County.
It has now burned more than 3,000 acres,
and officials say it's 35% contained.
This is NPR News.
A dangerous category for typhoon
passed 10 miles south of Guam on Saturday,
toppling trees and knocking out power,
but the island escaped major damage from that storm.
Dana Williams of member station KPRG reports from Guam.
- Emergency managers feared typhoon champion
would cause extensive damage in this U.S. territory,
but the storm's compact wind field
and relatively fast passage
prevented what could have been a major disaster.
Brandon Eidlut of the National Weather Service
says while the storm's eyewall packed winds
of 140 miles per hour,
gusts at the Guam airport just 20 miles away
barely exceeded 80 miles per hour.
He says shortly after the storm
made its closest point of approach,
Champy was upgraded to a super typhoon

- I don't know if you can split it closer than that,
having a super typhoon this close,
and not have impacts even 20 miles to the north.
- Champy is the third super typhoon recorded
in the Mariana Islands so far this year.
For NPR News, I'm Dana Williams on Guam.
- Today was a day for upsets in college football.
Auburn beat number one Georgia with a field goal
by Alex McPherson as time ran out, winning 27 to 24.
Unranked Florida beat number seven, Texas 27 to 24.

Number four, Ohio State University, meanwhile,
outlasted defending champion Indiana winning 19 to 15.
